text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- DEFICIT INCREASES TO 3.88 PCT OF GDP
Brazil's operational public sector deficit has risen to 3.88 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in August, compared with 3.7 percent of GDP in July.
-- BRASIL CENTRAL TO FLY TO UNITED STATES
TAM wants to be the fourth Brazilian airline to fly to the United States and is transforming its regional airline subsidiary Brasil Central into a national airline.
-- BRAZIL PAYS MORE FOR ITS GLOBAL BONUS
Brazil's first global bonus, which was launched yesterday, was priced higher than expected at 265 base points over U.S. Treasuries.
O GLOBO
-- STRAY BULLETS CLAIM TWO MORE VICTIMS

Stray bullets have claimed two more victims in Rio de Janeiro. A 10-year-old boy was shot in the leg at school and a 62-year-old woman was killed when a bullet hit her in the head while she was waiting at a busstop.
-- POLLUTION KILLS 1,000 CHILDREN A YEAR IN RIO
A World Bank survey on pollution in the state of Rio de Janeiro has found that 1,000 children die each year due to pollution related causes.
-- PRIEST ACCUSED OF SEX TRAFFICKING

Penthouse magazine is running a story on how a group of priests belonging to the New York Episcopal church have brought at least eight Brazilian young men to the United States in the past two years to satisfy their sexual desires.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- GOVT HOPES FOR 21 VOTES IN FAVOR OF RE-ELECTION
The government hopes 21 of the 30 members of a congressional committee discussing the presidential re-election issue will vote in favor of re-election.
-- PROSECUTOR TO CALL FOR EXHUMATION OF BABIES

A state prosecutor will call for the exhumation of 33 babies who died in a hospital in Boa Vista in the Amazonian state of Roraima to establish whether they died of an infection they contracted at the hospital.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
